newsitem.title: CHINA: China oil firm says disputed rig to stay.
newsitem.headline: China oil firm says disputed rig to stay.

text.p: China's main offshore oil company said on Thursday it had no immediate plans to move a drilling rig that has sparked a diplomatic row with Vietnam by operating in waters both countries claim.
"Any decision to leave the drilling area would be based on the drilling results," an official of the China National Offshore Oil Corp told Reuters.
"Why should we leave the area?" said the official. "When the exploration is finished we will move the rig."

Hanoi has called for immediate and unconditional meetings to resolve a territorial row sparked by China's decision to position the Kan Tan III exploration rig about 64.5 nautical miles off the coast of mainland central Vietnam.
Beijing said on Tuesday it was considering suggestions from Hanoi in the row, but gave no details of its plans for the rig.

The oil exploration dispute is the latest in a series of territorial disagreements between the two communist neighbours, which fought a brief but bloody border war in 1979 and clashed at sea in the 1980s.

Both sides have in recent years agreed to shelve some border problems and have worked hard to improve ties and boost border trade, but the temptation to exploit the oil-rich waters they dispute has been a constant threat to the rapprochement.
Hanoi turned up the heat this week in the latest row with its giant northern neighbour, accusing China of violating international laws and calling for urgent talks.
China responded that the area it was drilling was in its own territory and that its action was beyond reproach.
